title: China's imperial examination system
summary: China's civil service examinations began in the Sui dynasty (581–618) and were fully developed under the Qing. They were extremely difficult and required knowledge of the Confucian classics, law and government. By selecting candidates on merit, they weakened the hold of the hereditary aristocracy and created a class of scholar-officials. The Qing abolished them in 1905, after more than a thousand years.

uncertainty.note: Formal degree examinations began under the Sui dynasty (traditionally dated to Emperor Yang's institution of the jinshi examination in 605 CE) and operated until abolished by imperial decree in 1905.
